This one is for all the marbles.

At 8 p.m. ET, Trinity Rodman’s Washington Spirit take on Temwa Chawinga’s Kansas City Current in the 2026 NWSL Championship at Washington, D.C.’s Audi Field.

Tonight’s contest will be Washington’s third consecutive finals appearance after losing in 2024 and ’25 to the Orlando Pride and Gotham FC. Their last title was in 2021 when they took down the Chicago Red Stars 2-1.

As for Kansas City, they collected back-to-back titles in 2014 and ’15 when they were known as FC Kansas City. Their last return to the big dance was four years ago when the Portland Thorns FC defeated them.

Prior to this showdown, Washington and Kansas City last played on Oct. 25. The Current won 2-1 behind huge goals by Vanessa DiBernardo and Lo’eau LaBonta. Clara Luvanga scored the Spirit’s lone goal.

Dramatic body-camera footage captured the moment police in San Bernardino County pulled a teen from a burning car that overturned after colliding with a train.

Officers with the Colton Police Department responded to the crash near E. Steel Road and S. Hunts Lane late Wednesday night, the department said.

When officers arrived, they found a gray 2016 Mercedes-Benz sedan overturned and “engulfed in flames with the driver trapped inside” after being struck by an Amtrak train, according to the department and NBC Los Angeles.

In a clip shared by the department, an officer is seen pulling over after spotting the flaming car before rushing over to help.

“Hey, we got someone in here,” a cop can be heard saying.

The footage shows the officer crouching down after discovering the teen before pulling him out and dragging him to safety.

“Officers quickly worked to remove the driver from the burning vehicle and bring him to safety before rendering medical aid,” the department said.

“Colton Fire and paramedics responded, and the driver was transported to a local hospital. We are grateful for the swift actions of our officers and the coordinated response of Colton Fire and all personnel involved.”

The condition of the driver, described by NBC LA as an 18-year-old, was unclear.

A person who said they were on the train at the time of the crash recalled looking on as the wreck unfold.

“I saw the end of the car flip and land… It landed directly in front of me and two of my friends,” the person wrote on social media.

“We were in the observation car. One of my friends called 911 as soon as it happened. You guys showed up so fast… The whole thing was and still is very traumatizing…. “

The department said the cause of the crash was being investigated by railroad authorities.

Preparations for Miley Cyrus’ wedding were in full swing Saturday morning as staff put the finishing touches on a private residence in Palm Springs, California, where Page Six can confirm the nuptials are set to take place.

In new pictures, employees were seen carrying large, white floral arrangements into the location and unloading tons of boxes from various trucks.

Also seen in a picture was a pallet loaded with what looked like sod sheets.

Another photo also showed what appeared to be the reception tablescape, which was decorated with a white tablecloth, dark wooden chairs and white florals.

TMZ was first to report the location on Saturday.

The “Wrecking Ball” singer and her fiancé, Maxx Morando, are set to exchange their vows this weekend — and it looks like the two have already kicked off the celebrations.

In exclusive photos obtained by Page Six, the couple was spotted leaving their rehearsal dinner on Friday night.

Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, held hands and were both wearing all-black ensembles.

They were joined by Cyrus’ family, which included her mom, Tish, and younger sister, Noah.

Tish’s stepdaughter Lily-Rose Purcell also posted a sneak peek of what the rehearsal dinner looked like to her Instagram story. She shared a snap of the dinner table, which was decorated with crimson-colored flowers.

The photo also showed the couple’s rehearsal dinner menu, which included a first course of sherry cappuccino, potato pavé in brown butter and a pear and burrata mille-feuille with candied pecans and lavender vinaigrette.

The “Climb” hitmaker first debuted her engagement ring while walking the red carpet for the world premiere of “Avatar: Fire and Ash” last December.

Her ring was custom-made by jewelry designer Jacquie Aiche, which featured a cushion-cut stone set in a “chunky” 14-karat yellow gold band.

TMZ اولین رسانه‌ای بود که روز شنبه محل برگزاری مراسم را گزارش کرد. خواننده آهنگ «Wrecking Ball» و نامزدش، مکس موراندو، قرار است این آخر هفته پیمان ازدواج خود را ببندند — و به نظر می‌رسد که این دو نفر جشن‌ها را از قبل آغاز کرده‌اند. در عکس‌های انحصاری که Page Six به دست آورده است، این زوج در حال خروج از شام تمرینی خود در شب جمعه دیده شدند. سایرس 33 ساله و موراندو 28 ساله دست در دست هم داشتند و هر دو لباس‌های کاملاً مشکی پوشیده بودند. خانواده سایرس، از جمله مادرش، تیش، و خواهر کوچکترش، نوا، نیز به آنها پیوستند. لیلی-رز پورسل، دخترخوانده تیش، نیز تصویری کوتاه از نحوه برگزاری شام تمرینی را در استوری اینستاگرام خود منتشر کرد. او عکسی از میز شام را به اشتراک گذاشت که با گل‌های قرمز رنگ تزئین شده بود. در این عکس همچنین منوی شام تمرینی این زوج دیده می‌شد که شامل پیش‌غذای کاپوچینوی شری، سیب‌زمینی

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Fausto “Chapo Isidro” Meza Flores, one of Mexico’s most notorious drug kingpins and former rival of El Chapo, was arrested in a fiery joint Mexican-US operation that brought an end to the FBI’s long hunt for one of its 10 most wanted fugitives.

The 44-year-old is the alleged leader of the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, which is responsible for trafficking heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, and marijuana into the United States, according to the US State Department.

“The arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores marks another major hit to Mexican cartel leadership. For decades, Isidro maintained a powerful criminal presence across northern Sinaloa and southern Sonora,” Ray Donovan, former DEA Chief of Operations, told The Post.

“His influence stemmed from the Beltran Leyva organization, making him one of the region’s most entrenched drug traffickers. His capture highlights the importance of intelligence sharing and cooperation between US and Mexican authorities,” Donovan said.

Meza Flores began his career working for Amado Carillo Fuentes, the former head of the Juarez Cartel who died in 1997, according to Insight Crime.

Meza Flores later joined the Beltran Leyva Organization, which operated in Morelos and Sinaloa — acting as the right-hand man and high-level hitman for leader Alfredo Beltran Leyva. Mexican Special Forces arrested Leyva in 2008 and he was extradited to the United States in 2014, Insight Crime reported.

In 2008, the Beltran Leyva Organization split from the Sinaloa Cartel, run by the notorious kingpin Joaquin “El Chapo” Guzman, which resulted in prolonged bloody battles across Mexico that peaked in 2010.

After the collapse of the Beltran Leyva Organization, Meza Flores allegedly started his own cartel, the Meza-Flores Organization, also referred to as the Mazatlecos, which operates in Guasave and Sinaloa along the northwestern coast.

The US Department of the Treasury designated the group a Drug Trafficking Organization in 2013, saying that the “extremely violent” Mazatlecos were the main rival to the El Chapo-run Sinaloa Cartel.

“As a result of this rivalry, the Meza Flores DTO has engaged in an extremely violent turf war with the Sinaloa Cartel which has resulted in the quadrupling of drug-war killings in the last four years and an increase in kidnappings and arson within the state of Sinaloa,” the Treasury department said in a 2013 statement.

Meza Flores is allegedly responsible for the deaths of numerous Sinaloa State police officers, Mexican Military and law enforcement officials, as well as members of rival cartels, according to the US State Department.

He is also allegedly connected to the killings of 16 people, whose bodies were found burned in trucks in Culiacan in 2011, Insight Crime reported.

A warrant for Meza Flores’s arrest was issued by the US District Court for the District of Columbia in Washington, DC in 2019. He was also indicted on trafficking cocaine, marijuana, methamphetamine, as well as firearms violations.

The Meza-Flores organization was linked to the seizure of 20 million counterfeit fentanyl pills in December 2024. He was added to the FBI’s Top 10 Most Wanted list in February 2025, Insight Crime reported.

A new indictment was filed in September that saw him charged with narcoterrorism and conspiracy to provide material support to a terrorist group.

Meza Flores remains in custody in Mexico. No extradition date has been announced by authorities.

Experts say the high-profile arrest is a positive step but ending cartel activity remains the goal.

“Another significant victory, but dismantling the criminal networks behind these leaders remains the ultimate objective,” said Donovan.

news.originalContent:
Demonstrations in France and Portugal follow youth-led protests over education and economic hardship across Europe.

Thousands of people have taken to the streets across Europe to protest against rising living costs, unaffordable housing and cuts to public services, as students and workers demand action from their governments.

Demonstrators marched across France and Portugal on Saturday, following youth-led protests in several European countries on Friday.

The gatherings reflect overlapping concerns about economic insecurity, education and future opportunities, although their demands and scale differ considerably between countries.

In France, the Ministry of Interior said 82,500 people joined demonstrations nationwide on Saturday, including 21,500 in Paris, down from 106,000 the previous weekend. Organisers estimated a higher turnout of 150,000.

The protests, now in their sixth consecutive weekend, began in September with students demanding better schools before expanding to include trade unions and the Yellow Vests, a movement that emerged in 2018 over rising fuel prices and living costs.

Demonstrators have also criticised police violence and a new law strengthening protections for officers who use firearms.

In Portugal, thousands marched through Lisbon despite heavy rain, calling for higher wages, affordable housing and relief from rising prices.

The demonstration was organised by CGTP, the country’s largest trade union federation, which also demanded higher pensions and cheaper essential goods.

Portugal’s housing pressures have intensified as property prices have more than doubled since 2017.

Average annual earnings in 2025 were 37 percent below the European Union average, according to the EU’s statistics agency, Eurostat.

The weekend’s demonstrations followed Friday’s youth protests in Germany and Sweden.

About 4,000 people gathered in Berlin, while police reported roughly 200 participants at a Saturday march in Helsinki organised by left-wing and student groups.

Organisers of an international youth strike said demonstrations were planned in at least 25 countries, with demands ranging from greater education funding and climate action to opposition to compulsory military service.

In Germany, the youth campaign Gen Z regelt, meaning “Generation Z takes charge”, announced demonstrations in 73 locations.

In Italy, a nationwide strike organised by the CGIL, one of the country’s main trade union confederations, disrupted transport, schools and some healthcare services on Friday.

Demonstrations took place in more than 100 cities, with union leader Maurizio Landini claiming more than one million participants nationwide.

While some protests were linked through the international youth initiative, others grew out of established national campaigns, bringing different groups onto the streets over concerns about living standards and government spending.

Separately, thousands protested in the Croatian capital, Zagreb, on Saturday over the death of a man at a psychiatric hospital.

Four medical technicians are under investigation on suspicion of aggravated murder.
news.content: تظاهرات در فرانسه و پرتغال پس از اعتراضات جوانان به آموزش و مشکلات اقتصادی در سراسر اروپا برگزار می‌شود. هزاران نفر در سراسر اروپا به خیابان‌ها آمده‌اند تا به افزایش هزینه‌های زندگی، مسکن غیرقابل‌تحمل و کاهش خدمات عمومی اعتراض کنند، زیرا دانشجویان و کارگران خواستار اقدام دولت‌های خود هستند. تظاهرکنندگان روز شنبه در سراسر فرانسه و پرتغال راهپیمایی کردند. این راهپیمایی‌ها پس از تظاهراتی که روز جمعه با رهبری جوانان در چندین کشور اروپایی برگزار شد، صورت گرفت. این تجمعات نشان‌دهنده نگرانی‌های مشترک در مورد ناامنی اقتصادی، آموزش و فرصت‌های آینده است، اگرچه مطالبات و ابعاد این تظاهرات در کشورهای مختلف تفاوت قابل‌توجهی دارد. در فرانسه، وزارت کشور اعلام کرد که روز شنبه 82,500 نفر در سراسر کشور به تظاهرات پیوستند که 21,500 نفر از آنها در پاریس بودند؛ این رقم در مقایسه با 106,000 نفر در آخر هفته قبل کاهش یافته است. برآورد برگزارکنندگان از تعداد شرکت‌کنندگان بیشتر بود و 150,000 نفر تخمین زده شد. این تظاهرات که اکنون ششمین آخر هفته متوالی خود را سپری می‌کند، در ماه سپتامبر با مطالبه دانشجویان برای بهبود مدارس آغاز شد و سپس با پیوستن اتحادیه‌های کارگری و جنبش جلیقه‌زردها که در سال 2018 در اعتراض به افزایش قیمت سوخت و هزینه‌های زندگی شکل گرفت، گسترش یافت. تظاهرکنندگان همچنین خشونت پلیس و قانون جدیدی را که حمایت از مأمورانی که از سلاح گرم استفاده می‌کنند را تقویت می‌کند، مورد انتقاد قرار داده‌اند. در پرتغال، هزاران نفر علیرغم باران شدید در لیسبون راهپیمایی کردند و خواستار افزایش دستمزدها، مسکن ارزان و کاهش قیمت‌های رو به افزایش شدند. این تظاهرات توسط CGTP، بزرگترین فدراسیون اتحادیه‌های کارگری این کشور، سازماندهی شد که همچنین خواستار افزایش مستمری‌ها بود.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Managing the demands of work and keeping up with everything at home, it can feel like there are never enough hours in the day.

For busy, overscheduled families, hiring a house manager may be the key to reclaiming valuable time, reducing daily stress, and bringing a little more balance to everyday life.

For those who are unfamiliar with this trending form of home support, a house manager is basically someone who keeps track of things behind the scenes so you can off-load some of your never-ending to-do list.

“A house manager takes on the parts of the household a family chooses to hand off—that means both the everyday work and the planning behind it, from start to finish,” says Kelly Hubbell, founder and CEO of Sage Haus, a thriving house manager placement company. “Think meals, laundry, errands, calendars, pet care, and home projects. A house manager doesn’t just complete tasks … they anticipate what’s needed and handle it without being asked.”

In other words, a house manager is an added support system that helps keep a household functioning efficiently.

The simplest definition of a house manger is someone who helps facilitate everyday life behind the scenes.

“A housekeeper cleans, a nanny cares for the kids, a house manager owns whole areas of the household, from planning to follow-through,” says Hubbell.

There can be overlap. A house manager might tidy, do laundry, or prepare meals, depending on what the family hands off. The difference is ownership.

“Take laundry: A housekeeper might wash what’s in the basket, whereas a house manager who owns laundry knows the soccer uniform has to be clean by Saturday, without a reminder,” explains Hubbell. “The work that’s different is the thinking behind the household.”

The best house managers have sharp judgment and the ability to plan ahead, juggle several schedules and tasks at once, manage vendors, and make good decisions within the scope a family has agreed to, according to Hubbell.

They’re proactive and notice what needs attention before anyone asks. And because they’re in someone’s home, trust, reliability, and discretion are essential.

“People come to it from lots of backgrounds: nannies whose kids aged out of needing a nanny, teachers, hospitality and operations managers, military spouses who have set up a household in four cities, and moms coming back into the workforce after years of running their own homes—frankly, the hardest training there is,” says Hubbell, whose network now includes over 7,000 house managers in the U.S. and Canada, though Sage Haus accepts only about 5% of applicants to ensure quality.

“As AI changes the jobs available, this work depends on what technology can’t supply: human judgment, trust, and care,” she explains.

Basically, house managers are gaining traction because people are burning out, especially women.

“Most families hit a point where their life, career, or ambitions can’t grow any further without more support—I call that the support ceiling,” says Hubbell. “They don’t need to scale back their dreams. They need to scale up their support.”

Many families already have some help, like a cleaner every other week, a nanny/sitter, or groceries on autopilot. But someone still has to hold it all together—the noticing, planning, and following up.

“That’s the mental load, and research shows it usually stays with mom, even as her career and earnings grow,” says Hubbell.

According to a 2024 study from the University of Bath and the University of Melbourne, mothers in the U.S. carry 71% of mental-load tasks, and while women’s employment and earnings reduce their physical household labor, it does not shrink their cognitive burden.

“Real estate has always recognized the value of a well-maintained home. What we’re only beginning to recognize is the value of the work required to maintain it,” says Laura Marie Rivera, a gender equity and unpaid labor researcher and host of the “Motherhood Advantage” podcast. “The rise of professional house managers puts a job title and salary on responsibilities that mothers have managed for generations—largely without either.”

Unpaid household work in the U.S. is worth up to $6 trillion a year, and none of it shows up in the GDP. However, the rise of house mangers is finally putting a dollar amount on the mental load of keeping a home operational.

“Paying someone to manage a household doesn’t just reveal the economic value of the work, it reveals the scope of the work,” says Rivera. “We’re not witnessing the invention of a new profession so much as the professional recognition of work that has been hiding in plain sight.”

The good news is that having a house manager isn’t only for the wealthy. In general, cost depends on where you live and what you need the house manager to take on.

“Families hire and pay house managers directly, and pay ranges from $25 to more than $50 an hour depending on location and scope,” says Hubbell. “It doesn’t have to be full time: 80% of families start with part-time help, averaging 15 to 20 hours per week.”

For many families, a house manager can be a more practical investment than several separate kinds of help, because it brings that support together in one role. However, there are still options when budgetary constraints prohibit the employment of a house manager.

“Support doesn’t have to start with a hire,” says Hubbell. “It can begin with mapping out everything it takes to run your home and deciding what to drop, what to share with a partner, and where you need help most.”

That being said, for those who can swing it, having a house manager can be life-changing.

In theory this all sounds amazing, but what’s it like in practice? We checked in with a house manager and a family that’s hired a house manager to get the inside scoop. But the short version is, both are very happy with their decision.

Before becoming a house manager, Terry Boch worked as an executive assistant, but also spent years as a stay-at-home mom raising her three children.

Once they were grown and she reentered the work force, she was enjoying being an executive assistant again but realized she wanted something less computer-focused and more hands-on. That’s when she came across a job post seeking house managers. Intrigued, she pursued the opportunity, was matched with a family in New Jersey, and found it was a perfect fit for her skill set.

“I love transforming an already beautiful house into a warm, welcoming home that looks and smells inviting every day,” says Boch, whose primary responsibilities include meal planning, grocery shopping and meal preparation, laundry, resetting bedrooms and living spaces, and plant care. “I work approximately 15–20 hours per week, but I like to say that I get to play house in a home I could never afford.”

In reality, however, Boch says she sees what she does as much more about creating a home than maintaining a house.

“Although my interaction with the children is limited, knowing that I can contribute to an environment where they feel comfortable, cared for, and happy brings me tremendous joy,” says Boch. “I love making a home feel welcoming, anticipating what a family needs, and taking pride in all the little things that make everyday life more enjoyable. I’m not a house cleaner; I’m a homemaker at heart.”

On the flip side, Krissel Varela found her way to the idea of hiring a house manager online.

“Following Sage Haus on social media really opened my eyes to what household support could look like,” says Varela. “I had always thought about help in a more traditional sense, like a nanny or someone full-time, but started realizing we could shape the support around what our family actually needed.”

Though she’d had a nanny when her kids were younger and she was working a corporate job, once they reached school age, they didn’t need that kind of assistance anymore. However, their lives didn’t get less busy.

“Between school, sports, activities, keeping our household running, and now building a business of my own, there are just so many moving pieces,” says Varela. The idea of a house manager made sense for her family, though they didn’t need someone full time.

“Right now, we have help about 8 to 10 hours a week, and even though that’s not a huge number of hours, the impact feels so much bigger,” says Varela. Her house manager is usually with them on Mondays and Thursdays, with some flexibility predicated on their needs.

“Between laundry, household organization, errands, and all those little tasks that add up throughout the week, having someone share those responsibilities makes such a difference,” she adds.

Though it’s been only a few months, Varela says she can already feel a huge life shift.

“It’s not just the actual hours saved; it’s also the mental space that comes from knowing someone else is helping keep things moving without having to manage every little detail,” says Varela. “It’s also given me more room for the things that are easy to push aside when life gets busy, whether that’s spending quality time with my husband, enjoying our weekends, or even having a little time for myself. Having that extra support has really helped me be more intentional about where my time and energy go.”

And that is exactly what a house manager is supposed to do, open up space for life at home to be about more than just getting by every day.

“People should also know there’s a cost to getting support and a cost to going without it, whether that’s your health, your relationships, or your connection with your family,” says Hubbell. “The goal isn’t to outsource your life; it’s to get enough support to be present for it.”

Fresh off his posthumous pardon of baseball legend Pete Rose, President Trump turned his attention Saturday to two other Cooperstown outcasts — Barry Bonds and Roger Clemens — promising to “take a look” at their Hall of Fame snubs.

Trump made the remarks during a call-in interview with his former White House press secretary, Kayleigh McEnany, on Fox News’ “Saturday in America,” after she told him her husband, former Mets pitcher Sean Gilmartin, wanted to know whether Bonds belonged in the Major League Baseball Hall of Fame.

The president had granted Rose a posthumous pardon Thursday for tax violations, renewing attention on the Cincinnati Reds hit king’s exclusion from Cooperstown over his gambling scandal.

“It’s different. Pete didn’t take drugs,” Trump said, calling it “disgraceful” that he was not admitted to the Hall of Fame before he died in 2024.

“What Pete did is what they’re doing now – everyone’s gambling on sports, OK?” the president said in the call-in interview. “Pete only gambled on his own team.”

Rose, baseball’s all-time hits leader with 4,256, was banned from the sport in 1989 after an investigation found he had bet on baseball while managing the Reds. He later admitted betting on his own team to win. His lifetime ban kept him off the Hall of Fame ballot.

“Now the difference is Roger Clemens has never been proven to have taken drugs, and he swears that he didn’t,” Trump continued, referring to the seven-time Cy Young Award winner and former Yankees ace nicknamed “The Rocket.”

“And he went through committees and everything else, and that he actually won a court case. And Roger Clemens said and stated strongly he never took drugs. Barry Bonds, I think, said that, too. But a lot of, I mean, look, he was such a great player. You know, he was a great player before the so-called drug excursion, if that ever took place.”

“The problem is he – [it] just looks like he took drugs – I mean, but now he’s denied it, and Roger Clemens has strongly denied it.”

Bonds, who holds Major League Baseball’s career home run record with 762, and Clemens, who won 354 games, have both been denied entry to Cooperstown amid allegations involving performance-enhancing drugs.

Bonds acknowledged using substances supplied by the BALCO laboratory but maintained he did not knowingly take steroids. His 2011 obstruction-of-justice conviction was overturned by a federal appeals court in 2015.

Clemens was acquitted in 2012 of charges that he lied to Congress when he denied using performance-enhancing drugs.

“You know your baseball,” McEnany told Trump when the interview concluded.
news.content:
پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. رئیس جمهور ترامپ پس از عفو پس از مرگ اسطوره بیسبال، پیت رز، روز شنبه توجه خود را به دو طرد شده دیگر کوپرستاون - بری باندز و راجر کلمنس - معطوف کرد که قول داده بودند «نگاهی» به تالار مشاهیرشان بیندازند. ترامپ این اظهارات را طی مصاحبه ای با کیلی مک انانی، سخنگوی سابق کاخ سفید، در برنامه "شنبه در آمریکا" فاکس نیوز، پس از اینکه به همسرش، شان گیلمارتین، پارچ اسبق متس گفت، می خواهد بداند که آیا باندز متعلق به تالار مشاهیر لیگ بیسبال است یا خیر، بیان کرد. رئیس جمهور روز پنجشنبه پس از مرگ رز را به دلیل تخلفات مالیاتی مورد عفو قرار داده بود و توجه مجدد به محرومیت پادشاه تیم سینسیناتی ردز از کوپرستاون به دلیل رسوایی قمار او را دوباره جلب کرد. ترامپ گفت: "این متفاوت است. پیت مواد مخدر مصرف نمی کرد." الان چه می کنند - همه روی ورزش قمار می کنند، خوب؟ رئیس جمهور در این مصاحبه گفت: "پیت فقط روی تیم خودش قمار می کرد."
رز، رهبر تاریخ بیسبال با 4256 ضربه، در سال 1989 پس از تحقیقات نشان داد که او در زمان مدیریت قرمزها روی بیسبال شرط بندی کرده بود، از این ورزش محروم شد. او بعداً اعتراف کرد که روی تیم خودش برای برد شرط بندی کرده است. محرومیت مادام العمر او را از رای گیری تالار مشاهیر دور نگه داشت. ترامپ در ادامه با اشاره به 7-t ادامه داد: «اکنون تفاوت این است که راجر کلمنس هرگز ثابت نکرده است که مواد مخدر مصرف کرده است و او قسم می خورد که مصرف نکرده است.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Fresh off what it dubbed its “biggest election ever,” the Democratic Socialists of America is plotting a massive expansion of its political clout in 2028 — aiming to quadruple its presence in Congress to at least 32 House members while throwing its weight behind a White House contender.

“We’re going to run hundreds of socialists in 2028, we’re going to elect candidates up and down the ballot,” predicted Sarah Milner, a member of the DSA’s powerful National Political Committee, during a “Presidential Exploratory Committee Endorsement Launch Call” Wednesday night with members from around the country.

“Comrades, we are going to build the strongest socialist movement this country has ever seen. We’re going to overturn this whole corrupt system,” roared Milner, a self-described transgender Trotskyist, urging chapters to plan “DSA 101” sessions for an “influx of new members.”

The DSA officially kicked off its monthslong 2028 presidential nomination showdown last week, with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) widely expected to emerge the winner — and DSA leaders eager to ride the wave of a popular presidential pick.

“It’s a big selling point,” said Ashik Siddique, national DSA co-chair.

After encouraging Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) to run for president in 2016 but stopping short of backing him — saying it did not normally endorse presidential candidates — the DSA formally endorsed him for commander-in-chief in 2020.

But Bernie came second to President Biden in the Democratic primary, winning 28% of delegate votes to Sleepy Joe’s 68%.

“Even when Bernie Sanders ran in 2020 and didn’t become president, there was a massive coattail effect with DSA electing candidates locally all over the country. This time we can be even more intentional,” Siddique said.

“Our ideas are popular, that wasn’t always the case,” he gloated, pointing to surveys that showed 86% support for a higher minimum wage and 66% for government-provided health care — among others. “They’re things that when Bernie was campaigning on them a decade ago felt like a pipe dream.”

The DSA’s presidential pick will have to be loyal to socialism first, the leaders insisted.

“We are using the Democratic Party ballot line, but we don’t feel any fealty to the Democratic Party,” declared Ella Teevan, another National Political Committee member.

“We know the Democratic Party is the problem. We think eventually we might have enough contradictions with the Democratic Party that they don’t let us get away with this anymore.”

The DSA said it expects to announce its presidential endorsement next spring.

The socialist organization will go from two elected officials in the House of Representatives — AOC and fellow “squad” Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-MI) — to eight in January after the midterm wins.

They’ve added Reps.-elect Claire Valdez (D-NY), Darializa Avila Chevalier (D-NY), Chris Rabb (D-PA), Donavan McKinney (D-MI), Melat Kiros (D-CO) and Angela Gonzales-Torres (D-CA).
news.content:
در نتایج جستجوی خود، پوشش خبری بیشتری از ما را مشاهده کنید. سوسیالیست‌های دموکرات آمریکا که به تازگی «بزرگترین انتخابات تاریخ خود» را پشت سر گذاشته‌اند، در حال برنامه‌ریزی برای گسترش گسترده نفوذ سیاسی خود در سال 2028 هستند — هدف آنها این است که حضور خود در کنگره را چهار برابر کرده و حداقل 32 نماینده در مجلس نمایندگان داشته باشند و در عین حال از یک نامزد کاخ سفید حمایت کنند. سارا میلنر، عضو کمیته سیاسی ملی قدرتمند DSA، در «تماس آغازین تأیید کمیته اکتشافی ریاست‌جمهوری» که چهارشنبه شب با اعضایی از سراسر کشور برگزار شد، پیش‌بینی کرد: «در سال 2028 صدها سوسیالیست را نامزد خواهیم کرد و در تمام سطوح رأی‌گیری، نامزدها را انتخاب خواهیم کرد.»«رفقا، ما قوی‌ترین جنبش سوسیالیستی را که این کشور تا کنون به خود دیده است، ایجاد خواهیم کرد. میلنر که خود را یک تروتسکیست تراجنسیتی می‌داند، با صدای بلند گفت: «ما می‌خواهیم کل این سیستم فاسد را واژگون کنیم.» او از شاخه‌های حزب خواست تا جلسات «DSA 101» را برای «هجوم اعضای جدید» برنامه‌ریزی کنند.
DSA هفته گذشته به طور رسمی رقابت چندماهه خود برای نامزدی انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری 2028 را آغاز کرد. انتظار می‌رود که نماینده کنگره، الکساندریای اوکاسیو-کورتز (دموکرات از نیویورک)، برنده این رقابت باشد و رهبران DSA مشتاقند از موج محبوبیت یک نامزد ریاست‌جمهوری بهره ببرند. آشیک سیدیک، رئیس مشترک ملی DSA گفت: «این یک نقطه قوت بزرگ برای فروش است.» پس از تشویق سناتور برنی سندرز (مستقل-ورمونت) برای نامزدی در انتخابات ریاست جمهوری در سال 2016، اما عدم حمایت از او - با این استدلال که معمولاً از نامزدهای ریاست جمهوری حمایت نمی‌کند - DSA در سال 2020 به طور رسمی از او برای تصدی پست فرماندهی کل قوا حمایت کرد. اما برنی

news.originalContent:
The delayed blasts have stoked environmental fears and concerns about health effects in the state.

The United States Army is slated to conduct two controlled detonations at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in the Midwestern state of Iowa, aiming to destroy 68 drums of degraded lead azide — a highly volatile, lead-based explosive used to trigger the main charges in some conventional munitions.

Announced just five days before an original Friday, November 20, detonation date, the Army’s decision was authorised by an emergency permit issued by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

Residents, environmental health experts, and Iowa elected officials have decried the detonation of lead-rich explosive material, citing scant public notice and potential environmental and health harms.

In a statement posted on X on Thursday, Iowa Democratic Senator-elect Josh Turek stressed the need for greater transparency.

“Iowans deserve to know that every safety precaution has been taken and exactly what the associated health risks are. Until those questions are answered, the detonation should not proceed,” he wrote.

Mounting public pressure has prompted the military to push the controlled blasts back to Monday, November 23.

But a late-stage legal challenge has cast doubt on whether the army will be able to proceed at all.

On the eve of the originally scheduled operation, two Iowa environmental advocacy groups — the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter — petitioned a federal appeals court to overturn the EPA emergency permit, arguing that the agency had not given the public meaningful advance notice, failed to require adequate safeguards to protect human health and the environment, and sanctioned the operation without sufficient consideration of safer disposal alternatives.

Here’s what we know so far:

In a November 15 advisory, the US Army warned residents of Middletown, a southeastern Iowa city of about 360 people, that the emergency blasts would loft a dust plume containing “some lead”, accompanied by loud explosions and ground vibrations.

The army’s containment strategy centres on thoroughly drenching the soil above the existing igloo-like, earth-covered concrete magazines — where the chemicals have been stored — with water before and during the detonations to help suppress airborne dust and particles.

The magazines are ringed by sand-filled barriers rising roughly two storeys high, designed to eject the force of the blast vertically into the sky, rather than laterally across the surrounding landscape.

“These measures should reduce the amount of lead that migrates from the detonation through the air off the installation,” the advisory reads.

According to the military’s modelling predictions, the blasts will deliver elevated airborne lead levels, but will remain “below the level at which EPA would require protective actions be taken”.

That’s reassurance with a blind spot, experts say.

Patrick O’Shaughnessy, an environmental health professor at the University of Iowa, who will be monitoring the environmental fallout from the detonations, says that for all the assumed precision of the army’s modelling, its most consequential variable remains undisclosed to the public: precisely how much lead each explosion will propel into the air.

It is the very quantity that will shape the scale of the downwind exposure.

“The unprecedented aspect of it is that normally in the world of air pollution, we have some estimation of what’s called the emission factor, the emission strength. We know how many pounds per second will be distributed out into the air from a smokestack,” O’Shaughnessy told Al Jazeera, “but in this case, we have no idea.”

The longer-term, more invisible peril, O’Shaughnessy said, is lead settling on playground equipment, getting into crops, landing in back yards and on other play surfaces where people could be exposed.

During a safety review in March, technicians discovered a stockpile of deteriorating lead azide that had languished in storage bunkers for 20 years at its Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, a sprawling 19,000-acre installation in Des Moines County, about 16 kilometres (10 miles) west of the Mississippi River, which separates Iowa and the state of Illinois.

Since then, the Army says it has engaged with the local community, including at an open house at the Army Reserve Center in mid-October for residents within a 50-mile (80km) radius of the facility, where it outlined its developing plans to eliminate the explosive hazard.

The stockpile includes roughly 9,700 pounds (just under five tonnes) of the explosives across 68 barrels, set to be detonated in place — material that contains roughly 6,900 pounds (about 3.5 tonnes) of lead by chemical mass.

During long-term storage, liquid in the drums evaporated and caused the lead azide to recrystallise.

According to the environmental assessment for Lead Azide Risk Mitigation, prepared by the Army, the recrystallisation had heightened the material’s sensitivity to shock and friction.

“Due to its chemical degradation, the material’s legal status transitioned from a viable production component to an unserviceable hazardous waste,” the report states.

Army Sustainment Command spokesperson Justine Barati said the Army faced a narrowing window to destroy the chemical material before colder weather or disturbances increased the risk of spontaneous detonation, which would pose an unacceptable risk of killing technicians on-site.

“We’re trying to do a controlled detonation to minimise the impact to the community and the environment. This is not something that we take lightly. We know that this is a disruption to people and that is not our intent, but we’re trying to do this in the safest manner possible,” Barati told a local television news station earlier this week.

Lead azide is an inorganic chemical compound made of lead and nitrogen, with lead accounting for about 71 percent of its mass.

Elemental lead cannot be destroyed by heat. It decomposes, melts, vaporises or fragments into fine particulate dust.

“Everyone should be shocked to learn this problem has been left long enough to warrant the potential catastrophic fallout from this situation,” said Dr Aaron Specht, an associate professor at Purdue University’s School of Health Sciences.

A fact sheet issued by the Army in advance of the scheduled disposal asserts that the heat generated by a proper detonation “incinerates” the lead azide.

Bruce Lanphear, a paediatric epidemiologist and professor of health sciences at Simon Fraser University, disputed the chemistry explanation.

“When lead azide detonates, it decomposes primarily into nitrogen gas and lead,” he told Al Jazeera, “the lead may be released as fine particles of metallic lead, lead oxides, and other lead compounds. The explosion doesn’t destroy the lead. It redistributes it.”

The risks of lead exposure are particularly pronounced for fetuses exposed in utero through the mother’s bloodstream, as well as the pregnant women themselves. Young children, whose developing nervous systems are acutely susceptible to lead, are also at risk. Because of their smaller body mass, comparatively little lead is required to reach biologically significant doses in children.

Lead can cause serious harm even below regulatory limits.

There is no blood level of lead in a child that is deemed safe, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Lanphear has spent four decades studying how even low-level lead exposure can severely blunt children’s cognitive function.

“The danger of lead exposure as a distinct threat has been known for over a hundred years,” said Lanphear, “the neurotoxin causes permanent neuropsychological and developmental injuries … lower IQ, less tolerance for frustration, ADHD, and weak executive control functions.”

At high doses, lead poisoning can precipitate encephalopathy, a severe disturbance of brain function, or induce premature death.

Lead also figures prominently in cardiovascular mortality, said Lanphear, who co-authored a 2018 study estimating that long-term lead exposure was linked to 412,000 deaths annually across the US, including 256,000 deaths from cardiovascular disease.

While the original detonation was scheduled for Friday, Army acting Secretary Adam R Telle announced on social media Thursday night that the operation would be postponed until Monday, which he described as “the latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material”.

The Army did not announce a time for the deferred blasts.

Later on Thursday, in response to the Iowa groups’ lawsuit, the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit granted an interim stay of the EPA’s emergency authorisation, temporarily blocking the military from proceeding while the court weighed the groups’ request for a longer-term injunction.

It is an interim measure, not a final ruling on the legality of the permit.

The Army cannot technically detonate the chemicals under its EPA permit while the suspension remains in force, but the court may lift the pause beforehand.

While the court has put the brakes on the planned detonation for now, Justice Department lawyers, on Friday, pointed to separate emergency powers that the federal government could still invoke to bypass the permit requirement and press ahead with the blasts.
news.content: این انفجارهای تأخیری باعث ایجاد ترس‌های زیست‌محیطی و نگرانی‌ها در مورد اثرات سلامتی در این ایالت شده است. ارتش ایالات متحده قرار است دو انفجار کنترل‌شده در کارخانه مهمات ارتش آیووا در ایالت غرب میانه آیووا انجام دهد که هدف آن از بین بردن 68 طبل از آزید سرب تخریب‌شده است - یک منفجره اصلی منفجره و منفجره که در برخی از سرب‌ها استفاده می‌شود. مهمات تصمیم ارتش که فقط پنج روز قبل از روز انفجار اصلی جمعه، 20 نوامبر، اعلام شد، با مجوز اضطراری صادر شده توسط آژانس حفاظت از محیط زیست ایالات متحده (EPA) تایید شد. ساکنان، کارشناسان بهداشت محیط و مقامات منتخب آیووا انفجار مواد منفجره غنی از سرب را با استناد به مضرات عمومی ناچیز و مضرات بهداشتی بالقوه محیط‌زیست محکوم کرده‌اند. جاش تورک، سناتور منتخب دموکرات آیووا، در بیانیه‌ای که روز پنج‌شنبه در روز X منتشر شد، بر نیاز به شفافیت بیشتر تاکید کرد. "آیوان‌ها شایسته دانستن این هستند که همه اقدامات احتیاطی ایمنی اتخاذ شده است و دقیقاً چه خطراتی برای سلامتی مرتبط است. تا زمانی که به این سوالات پاسخ داده نشود، انفجار نباید ادامه یابد." او نوشت. اما یک چالش قانونی در مرحله آخر تردیدهایی را در مورد اینکه آیا ارتش اصلاً قادر به ادامه کار خواهد بود یا خیر ایجاد کرده است. در آستانه عملیات برنامه ریزی شده اولیه، دو گروه حامی محیط زیست آیووا - شورای محیط زیست آیووا و فصل آیووا در باشگاه سیرا - درخواست کردند.

(Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

The Trump administration is keeping a Michigan coal plant available into winter while it asks an appeals court to revisit a ruling against it.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright ordered the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, which runs the Midwest grid, and Consumers Energy to have the J.H. Campbell plant, in West Olive, Michigan, available to run through Feb. 12, 2027, the Energy Department announced Nov. 14. Emergency orders for seven other power plants in six states end between Nov. 20 and Dec. 31, the department’s records show.

“Ensuring coal plants such as the Campbell Plant are available to operate has prevented blackouts and likely saved lives,” Wright said in the release. “Americans deserve access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity regardless of whether the wind is blowing or the sun is shining.”

The order directs the grid operator to use economic dispatch, running Campbell only when the emergency requires it and keeping costs down, the department said.

Midwest grid operator media relations adviser McKenzie Barbknecht said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation that plants kept open under the orders “are dispatched like any other resource – through economic dispatch to meet system needs at the lowest cost.”

The grid operator “does not disclose unit specific generation information,” Barbknecht said.

It is the first Campbell order since Sept. 11, when the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit struck down Wright’s original emergency order for the plant. The department has asked the court to rehear the case, and that request is still pending, Utility Dive reported on Nov. 16.

The court threw out only the first Campbell order and has not reviewed the orders that followed it, the American Public Power Association noted in October. (RELATED: Trump’s Energy Department Keeps Ordering Coal Plants To Stay Open After Losing In Court)

The first of the other orders, for Units 3 and 4 at Constellation Energy’s Eddystone Generating Station in Pennsylvania, was scheduled to end Nov. 20. Orders for plants in Florida, Washington, Indiana and Colorado run out over the following five weeks.

Constellation said in a statement to the DCNF that it “will continue to keep Eddystone Units 3 and 4 operational for as long as the DOE 202 Orders remain in force.”

Since Aug. 23, 2026, both units ran Sept. 1-3, Unit 3 ran again Sept. 4 and Unit 4 ran Oct. 14. Operating the two units cost about $4.9 million in the order’s first term, from May 31 to Aug. 28, 2025, and $5.1 million in its second, the company said. When it sought repayment from PJM Interconnection, which runs the mid-Atlantic grid, Constellation deducted the net revenue the units earned.

The department renewed its order for Unit 4 at Talen Energy’s Wagner Generating Station in Anne Arundel County, Maryland, on Nov. 17, the day the previous order ended, its website shows. The new order runs about six weeks, through Dec. 31, after two 90-day terms.

PJM applied for the order after the unit ran out of its allowed operating hours during a summer heat spell, the department said in a Nov. 18 release.

“The Trump Administration is committed to keeping the lights on and ensuring American families and businesses have access to affordable, reliable, and secure power,” a department spokesperson said in a statement to the DCNF.

“At the request of PJM, the Energy Department took decisive action to strengthen grid reliability and ensure Americans across the mid-Atlantic region have a dependable power grid that delivers electricity when they need it most,” the spokesperson added.

Talen and the Michigan attorney general’s office did not respond to the DCNF’s requests for comment.

Consumers expects to ask the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to let it recover $303 million in costs under the orders through Sept. 30, “including amounts already requested,” after applying $344 million in revenue from the Midwest grid operator, the company said in its quarterly filing.

Consumers spokesman Brian Wheeler said in a statement to the DCNF that the company would not “speculate on future costs.” He said Consumers has asked federal regulators “to allow us to recover most of those costs for the first three 90-day periods from customers in 10 other Midwest states who benefited from that power.”

“Those cases are pending. We will submit additional cost recovery filings for costs incurred complying with all subsequent 90-day periods,” Wheeler said.

The utility wants ratepayers in 11 states, from Michigan and Illinois to Montana and the Dakotas, to cover the plant’s costs, the Environmental Defense Fund said, according to Utility Dive.

Wheeler said the utility “will continue to follow the law and operate our Campbell plant,” Utility Dive reported. “Consistent with these emergency orders, we will work to ensure that everyone who benefits from power from the Campbell plant across the Midwest pays their fair share.”

“Coal-fired power plants have become a political football. Democrats want to shut them down, Republicans want to keep them running indefinitely, and the political pendulum keeps on swinging,” Travis Fisher, director of energy and environmental policy studies at the Cato Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF.

“This is an irrational way to manage the electricity grid, and consumers are left dealing with the consequences. The answer is to get politics out of electricity decisions, rather than forcing ratepayers to pay for Washington’s latest intervention,” Fisher added.

Jordan Nader, a resident senior fellow for energy and environment at the R Street Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF that the new order does not meet the guardrails his colleague Michael Giberson called for in May.

Those guardrails “should be transparent, based on cost-benefit analysis, and demonstrate consideration of alternatives,” Nader said.

The Midwest grid operator should spread Campbell’s costs across its region when it calls on the plant, he said.

“It would be improper to isolate the costs and allocate them only to Michigan,” he added.

The department still says the plant is needed. It cited a report by federal regulators and the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, saying the Arctic cold of winter 2026, including Winter Storm Fern, showed the grid needs plants that can run on demand.

Environmental and consumer groups say there is no emergency, Utility Dive reported.

“Someone will be left holding the financial bag,” Environmental Law & Policy Center CEO Howard Learner said in a statement reported by Utility Dive.

The Sierra Club’s Jessi Eidbo called the order “yet another illegal and expensive extension,” the Associated Press reported on Nov. 16.

“The Trump Administration’s unlawful actions have created a horribly expensive mess with no easy answer for who pays for it,” Karlee Weinmann, research and communications manager at the utility watchdog Energy and Policy Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF.

Democratic Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel said on Nov. 17 she would ask the department to rehear the new order. Her office has filed six such requests and six petitions with the D.C. Circuit, according to a Nov. 17 press release from her office.

“In September, a federal court ruled DOE’s first Campbell plant order was entirely illegal, and this seventh order makes no further effort to comply with the law,” Nessel said.

“My office will continue to pursue every measure and remedy available to us as we seek, for the people of Michigan, relief from these continuing unlawful orders which keep an obsolete coal-plant burning to the detriment of our state residents,” Nessel added.

“Green zealots like to call the power situation a ‘fabricated emergency’ because the power always seems to work just fine at their house. They expect us to forget winter storm Fern when grid operators declared a real emergency because they were in need of power generation,” Larry Behrens, communications director of Power The Future, said in a statement to the DCNF.

“The Campbell plant delivered critical energy when Michigan needed it the most, and no doubt if there were blackouts Dana Nessel would’ve been among the first to blame the Trump Administration. Nessel’s tired response is always the same: shut down a working plant, kill jobs, and hope the weather cooperates,” he added.

Closing Campbell would pull “needed energy off the grid as the coldest time of the year approaches,” Behrens said.

“This winter, families and businesses will need baseload plants like Campbell for lighting and heating,” Ted Ellis, deputy director of energy and environment policy at the America First Policy Institute, said in a statement to the DCNF.

“Secretary Wright is delivering an America First policy solution to a real problem on the ground: reliable power plants, including coal generation, are being retired before dependable replacements exist,” Ellis added.

Consumers had planned to close the 64-year-old plant on May 31, 2025, which the department says was 15 years short of its design life. The Nov. 13 order is the seventh for the plant since May 2025, the AP reported.

The next order to expire after Eddystone covers Unit 1 at the Stanton Energy Center in Orlando, Florida, on Nov. 30.

دولت ترامپ در حالی که از دادگاه تجدیدنظر می‌خواهد تا حکمی را که علیه آن صادر شده است، مورد بررسی مجدد قرار دهد، یک نیروگاه زغال‌سنگ در میشیگان را تا زمستان فعال نگه می‌دارد. وزارت انرژی در نوامبر اعلام کرد که کریس رایت، وزیر انرژی، به اپراتور مستقل سیستم میدکانتیننت که شبکه برق غرب میانه را اداره می‌کند و همچنین به شرکت Consumers Energy دستور داده است که نیروگاه J.H. Campbell در وست الیو، میشیگان، تا 12 فوریه 2027 فعال باشد. 14. طبق سوابق این وزارتخانه، دستورات اضطراری برای هفت نیروگاه دیگر در شش ایالت بین 20 نوامبر تا 31 دسامبر به پایان می‌رسد.رایت در این بیانیه گفت: «اطمینان از آمادگی نیروگاه‌های زغال‌سنگ مانند نیروگاه کمپبل برای بهره‌برداری، از خاموشی‌ها جلوگیری کرده و احتمالاً جان افراد را نجات داده است.» «آمریکایی‌ها شایسته دسترسی به برق ارزان، قابل‌اعتماد و ایمن هستند، صرف‌نظر از اینکه باد می‌وزد یا خورشید می‌تابد.» این اداره اعلام کرد که این دستور، اپراتور شبکه را ملزم می‌کند از اعزام اقتصادی استفاده کند، نیروگاه کمپبل را فقط در مواقع اضطراری و در صورت لزوم راه‌اندازی کند و هزینه‌ها را کاهش دهد. مک‌کنزی بارب‌کنشت، مشاور روابط رسانه‌ای اپراتور شبکه غرب میانه، در بیانیه‌ای به Daily Caller News Foundation گفت که نیروگاه‌هایی که طبق این دستورات باز نگه داشته می‌شوند «مانند هر منبع دیگری - از طریق اعزام اقتصادی برای تأمین نیازهای سیستم با کمترین هزینه - اعزام می‌شوند.» بارب‌نِخت گفت: «اپراتور شبکه اطلاعات مربوط به تولید هر واحد را افشا نمی‌کند.» این اولین دستور کمپبل از 11 سپتامبر است، زمانی که دادگاه استیناف ایالات متحده برای ناحیه کلمبیا

news.originalContent:
League leaders Arsenal miss the chance to go eight points clear of second placed Brighton, who play on Sunday.

Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw.

The Gunners led on Saturday through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.

But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.

However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.

Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.

Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second-half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St James’ Park.

Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title.

Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a 75 million pound ($98m) move to the Emirates Stadium in August.

The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener.

It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.

Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.

Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.

Suddenly, an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.

Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.

That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.

But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.

Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the righ,t and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.

Madueke told Sky Sports that he thought 2-2 was a “fair” result.

“Game of two halves is fair. First half we were outstanding. Should have got three goals, to be honest. Missed a couple of chances myself. Everything else was there,” he said.

“The second half, the first 20 minutes, was not good by our standard. When you give this team and crowd belief at home, it is difficult. We showed character to get back in the game, but 2-2 is a fair result.”
news.content: آرسنال، رهبران لیگ، فرصت هشت امتیاز اختلاف با برایتون رده دومی را که یکشنبه بازی می‌کند، از دست داد. آرسنال پس از یک مبارزه هیجان‌انگیز در نیمه دوم از نیوکاسل، مدافع عنوان قهرمانی را به تساوی 2-2 رساند. اما مردان میکل آرتتا ناگهان به سمت شکست پیش رفتند که گل‌های هاروی بارنز و مالیک تیاو، تقویت بسیار مورد نیاز را برای ماتیاس جیسل، سرمربی نیوکاسل فراهم کرد. نونی مادوکه یک امتیاز را برای آرسنال نجات داد و برتری خود را در بالای جدول نسبت به بسته شگفت‌انگیز برایتون به 6 امتیاز افزایش داد. در مسابقه قهرمانی که بسیاری معتقد بودند آرسنال به آن دست خواهد یافت. نیوکاسل با تنها یک برد در شش بازی در تمامی رقابت‌ها در نیمه انتهایی جدول باقی می‌ماند. با این حال، جیسل می‌تواند به عملکرد تیمش در نیمه دوم به عنوان یک نقطه عطف بالقوه پس از شروع دشوار سلطنتش در سنت جیمز پارک اشاره کند. آرسنال با فاصله 6 امتیازی نسبت به منچسترسیتی رده سومی فاصله دارد، اما این فرصت را از دست داد تا پای خود را در دفاع از عنوان قهرمانی خود پایین بیاورد. مادوکه در غیاب بوکایو ساکا با مصدومیت به فرم چشمگیر خود ادامه داد و زود به تیر دروازه زد. برونو گیماراس کاپیتان سابق نیوکاسل در اولین بازگشتش به تاین ساید پس از انتقال 75 میلیون پوندی (98 میلیون دلاری) به ورزشگاه امارات به شدت هو شد.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Justin TALLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

Hackers reportedly breached a Federal Bureau of Investigation database which tracks fugitives and monitors sex offenders Saturday in what could be the second cyberattack against the agency in months.

The FBI is investigating the breach of its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), though it is unclear what information has been compromise, Fox News reported, citing three sources familiar with the situation. (RELATED: FAA Lets Flights Resume After Hours-Long Ground Stop. Mullin Says Disruption Wasn’t A ‘Nefarious Attack.’)

The FBI did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment.

President Donald Trump told Fox News’s Kayleigh McEnany in a Saturday morning interview that he “just heard” of the breach.

“I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump said. “But maybe we’ll learn things that we wouldn’t have learned otherwise, because, yeah, you know you had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all of these other hoaxes … maybe we’ll learn about them.”

The apparent breach follows a Sept. 22 cyberattack by the ShinyHunters criminal hacking group which took down the FBI’s online job portal. FBI Director Kash Patel later announced Oct. 9 that the FBI arrested one of the suspects.

“This is the latest arrest this FBI has made in a matter of days involving this network, as we work non-stop to dismantle the group, pursue new leads and evidence, and act quickly,” Patel wrote on X. “We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what’s left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate.”

Trump replaced U.S. National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross on Thursday after a series of technological disruptions rattled systems used across the nation. Notably, Microsoft Outlook faced a 36-hour outage Nov. 12, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop Nov. 13, and hackers spread malware to 178 major websites Tuesday.
news.content:
(عکس از جاستین تالیس / خبرگزاری فرانسه از طریق گتی ایماژ)
گزارش‌ها حاکی از آن است که هکرها به پایگاه‌داده‌ای اداره تحقیقات فدرال که فراریان را ردیابی می‌کند و مجرمان جنسی را زیر نظر می‌گیرد، در حمله سایبری که می‌تواند دومین حمله سایبری علیه آژانس در چند ماه اخیر باشد، نقض کردند. فاکس نیوز به نقل از سه منبع آگاه گزارش داد که FBI در حال تحقیق در مورد نقض مرکز اطلاعات جرایم ملی خود (NCIC) است، اگرچه معلوم نیست چه اطلاعاتی به خطر افتاده است. (مرتبط: FAA اجازه می دهد پروازها پس از ساعت ها توقف زمینی از سر گرفته شوند. مولین می گوید اختلال یک "حمله شرورانه" نبود.)
اف‌بی‌آی بلافاصله به درخواست پایگاه خبری دیلی کالر برای اظهارنظر پاسخ نداد. دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در مصاحبه صبح روز شنبه به کایلی مک‌انانی، خبرنگار فاکس نیوز، گفت که «به‌تازگی درباره این نقض‌شناختی شنیده است.» ترامپ گفت: «من می‌گویم که خوب نیست. من این را دوست ندارم». "اما شاید چیزهایی یاد بگیریم که در غیر این صورت یاد نمی‌گرفتیم، زیرا، بله، شما می‌دانید که شما حقه‌بازی روسیه، روسیه، روسیه را داشتید. شما همه این حقه‌های دیگر را داشتید... شاید ما در مورد آنها یاد بگیریم."
نقض آشکار به دنبال یک سپتامبر است. 22 حمله سایبری توسط گروه هکر جنایی ShinyHunters که پورتال شغلی آنلاین FBI را از بین برد. کش پاتل، مدیر اف‌بی‌آی، بعداً در 9 اکتبر اعلام کرد که اف‌بی‌آی یکی از مظنونان را دستگیر کرده است. پاتل در X نوشت: «این آخرین دستگیری این اف‌بی‌آی در چند روز اخیر است که این شبکه را درگیر کرده است، زیرا ما بی‌وقفه برای متلاشی کردن گروه، تعقیب سرنخ‌ها و شواهد جدید و اقدام سریع تلاش می‌کنیم».

خبرگزاری تابناک در واکنش به این ویدیو نوشت «صرفه‌جویی با ناتوانی در تامین انرژی یکی نیست و ساده‌زیستی هم نباید جایگزین پاسخ‌گویی شود.» و آن را «به جای نماد مدیریت بحران، سهل‌انگاری مسئولیت دولت در تامین نیازهای اساسی مردم دانست.»

بعضی هم انتشار این تصاویر را آماده‌سازی جامعه برای قطع شدن برق و گاز در فصل سرما می‌دانند.

آقای پزشکیان ۲۸ آبان ۱۴۰۵ نیز در همایش بسیج دانشجویی در دانشگاه تهران، با اشاره به ضرورت صرفه‌جویی در انرژی گفته بود «با کاپشن می‌خوابد و در خانه‌اش برق و گرمایش روشن نمی‌کند.»

این صحبت‌های آقای پزشکیان هم واکنش‌برانگیز شد.  بعضی با تصاویر طنز از خوابیدن او با کاپشن، به وضعیت معیشت انتقاد کردند. بعضی هم این صحبت‌ها را پایین آوردن سطح توقع مردم از زندگی و دولت دانستند.

همچنین یکی از مخاطبان بی‌بی‌سی هم با کنایه به این صحبتها پیاده رفتن سرکار، پوشیدن لباس بیشتر در فصل سرما و کمتر غذا خوردن  را راه حل‌های رئیس‌جمهور برای مسائل کشور دانست.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images

A federal judge has barred Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins from sending religious holiday messages to her entire workforce.

U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson granted a preliminary injunction Thursday after concluding that Rollins’s Christmas and Easter emails to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) staff likely crossed into unconstitutional coercion, according to The Hill. Thompson, appointed by President Biden, wrote that the secretary’s “good faith intentions … are not the issue here” and that the two messages “go too far.”

The ruling faults Rollins for using her authority to push faith on subordinates, Raw Story reported. Thompson rejected the government’s position that employees could simply disregard the emails, calling that argument one that “defies logic.” (RELATED: Autists, Diabetics Sue Trump Admin To Restore EBT Welfare Benefits For Junk Food)

She also pointed to a USDA policy, Secretary’s Memorandum 1078-019, noting a rank-and-file worker probably could not blast the whole agency with an unsolicited appeal to fast for Ramadan or attend synagogue, and she questioned why the secretary should get a pass.

A US judge ordered Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to stop sending religious emails to employees from her official account, saying Rollins ‘must recognize’ boundaries when communicating religious messages and that some of her word choices assumed that email recipients subscribed to her Christian beliefs https://t.co/XTVVsWLlRX

Rollins sent the disputed messages from her official account, The Hill reported. The April email opened with “Happy Easter — He is Risen indeed!” and told employees that God had “granted each of us victory and new life.” It likened staff to “the very first disciples to encounter our risen Lord in the Upper Room almost two thousand years ago.”

A pre-Christmas video described Jesus as a savior who came “to free us from our sins,” Fox News reported, and a July 4 message asked for God’s protection over the country.

The National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE) and seven workers filed the suit in May in California, Religion News Service reported. The plaintiffs include Jewish, Buddhist, pagan and atheist staffers who said the messages left them feeling excluded. Americans United for Separation of Church and State, Democracy Forward and Bryan Schwartz Law represented them.

USDA offered no defense of the emails, telling Fox News it does not comment on pending litigation but would “keep the plaintiffs in our prayers.” Rollins, who posts Scripture online and joins Cabinet Bible studies, responded on X that the case was “just another opportunity to remind everyone: He is Risen.”

Thompson dismissed related claims under the Administrative Procedure Act and left Rollins free to practice her faith privately, Raw Story reported.
news.content:
عکس از الکس وانگ/Getty Images
یک قاضی فدرال بروک رولینز، وزیر کشاورزی، را از ارسال پیام‌های مربوط به اعیاد مذهبی به کل کارکنان خود منع کرده است. به گزارش The Hill، قاضی منطقه ایالات متحده، ترینا تامپسون، روز پنجشنبه پس از این نتیجه‌گیری که ایمیل‌های کریسمس و عید پاک رولینز به کارکنان وزارت کشاورزی ایالات متحده (USDA) احتمالاً به اجبار غیرقانونی تبدیل شده است، یک حکم موقت صادر کرد. تامپسون که توسط رئیس‌جمهور بایدن منصوب شده است، نوشت که «نیت خیرخواهانه وزیر … موضوع مورد بحث در اینجا نیست» و این دو پیام «بیش از حد افراطی هستند».
طبق گزارش Raw Story، این حکم رولینز را به دلیل استفاده از اختیاراتش برای تحمیل اعتقادات مذهبی به زیردستانش مقصر می‌داند. تامپسون موضع دولت مبنی بر اینکه کارکنان می‌توانند به سادگی این ایمیل‌ها را نادیده بگیرند، رد کرد و این استدلال را «مغایر با منطق» خواند. » (موضوع مرتبط: افراد مبتلا به اوتیسم و دیابت از دولت ترامپ شکایت می‌کنند تا مزایای رفاهی EBT برای غذاهای ناسالم را بازگرداند)
او همچنین به سیاست وزارت کشاورزی ایالات متحده، یادداشت شماره 1078-019 وزیر اشاره کرد و خاطرنشان کرد که احتمالاً یک کارمند عادی نمی‌تواند کل سازمان را با درخواست ناخواسته برای روزه‌داری در ماه رمضان یا حضور در کنیسه تحت فشار قرار دهد و سؤال کرد که چرا وزیر باید از این قاعده مستثنی باشد. یک قاضی آمریکایی به Brooke Rollins، وزیر کشاورزی، دستور داد که ارسال ایمیل‌های مذهبی به کارمندان از حساب رسمی خود را متوقف کند و گفت که Rollins «باید» در هنگام ارسال پیام‌های مذهبی، مرزها را رعایت کند و برخی از انتخاب‌های کلامی او نشان می‌دهد که فرض کرده است گیرندگان ایمیل با اعتقادات مسیحی او موافق هستند https://co/url/1/

news.originalContent:
The reported hacking is the latest in ​a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.

The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.

President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly downplayed breaches affecting departments within his administration, appeared to confirm the FBI hacking during a television interview on Saturday.

“Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump told Fox News.

On Friday, CNN and NBC reported that the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share information on criminal warrants and background checks, was compromised, citing two people who had been briefed on the matter.

The reported hacking, which would be the second to hit the bureau this year, is the latest in a string of US government breaches and outages that have alarmed officials over the past week.

In a separate incident, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture.

The FBI and USDA did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.

In the interview on Saturday, Trump suggested the hack of the FBI’s crucial database could be viewed with “a positive spin”.

“Maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise. You had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all these other hoaxes,” he said in an apparent reference to his discontent with the FBI’s investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 US election.

In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber group that claimed it had stolen sensitive information on the bureau’s 38,000 employees.

Additionally, in March, the agency said it had been investigating “suspicious activities” on some of its internal systems, The Associated Press news agency reported.

FBI Director Kash Patel, who has not publicly commented on the most recent hacking, was not present for a Wednesday hearing at the US Capitol to examine threats against the US. Patel’s deputy, Christopher Raia, attended in his place, joining US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.
news.content: هک گزارش شده جدیدترین مورد از یک رشته نقض و قطعی است که دولت ایالات متحده را تحت تأثیر قرار می دهد. طبق گزارش های متعدد رسانه های ایالات متحده، پایگاه داده جنایی ملی FBI دچار نقض مشکوک شده است. رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ، که بارها نقض های مربوط به بخش های داخل دولت خود را کم اهمیت جلوه داده است، به نظر می رسد هک FBI در روز شنبه طی یک مصاحبه تلویزیونی تایید کرده است. ترامپ به فاکس نیوز گفت: «خب، ما به تازگی در مورد آن شنیدیم و من می گویم که خوب نیست. من این را دوست ندارم.» روز جمعه، CNN و NBC گزارش دادند که مرکز ملی اطلاعات جرایم (NCIC) که توسط سازمان های مجری قانون در سراسر ایالات متحده برای به اشتراک گذاشتن اطلاعات در مورد حکم های جنایی و بررسی سوابق استفاده می شود، با استناد به دو نفر که در مورد این موضوع مطلع شده بودند، به خطر افتاد. این هک گزارش شده، که دومین موردی است که در سال جاری به این اداره وارد می شود، آخرین مورد از یک سری نقض ها و قطعی های دولت ایالات متحده است که مقامات را در هفته گذشته نگران کرده است. در یک رویداد جداگانه، NBC یک حمله سایبری آشکار علیه وزارت کشاورزی ایالات متحده را گزارش کرد. FBI و USDA بلافاصله درخواست الجزیره را برای اظهار نظر پاسخ ندادند. در مصاحبه روز شنبه، ترامپ پیشنهاد کرد که هک پایگاه داده مهم FBI را می توان با یک "چرخش مثبت" نگریست. او در اشاره ای آشکار به نارضایتی خود از T گفت: "شاید چیزهایی یاد بگیریم که در غیر این صورت هرگز نمی آموختیم.

Image not from story. (Photo by JOHANNES EISELE/AFP via Getty Images)

After the Nasdaq Composite index lost all of its 2026 gains Friday, multiple Wall Street analysts attributed the markets’ declines to the risks inherent in the financial viability of artificial intelligence investments.

U.S. stock markets ended the week amid the largest sell-off since President Donald Trump’s April 2025 Liberation Day tariffs, The Washington Post reported. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% on Friday alone, while the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped at least 8% over the week. Having entered correction territory, the indexes are each down at least 10% from recent highs. (RELATED: Wall Street Has AI-Induced Bloodbath As Exchange Has Worst Day Of Year)

“In my 25 years-plus investing in the markets, this is the most sentiment-driven sell-off I’ve seen,” Founders 100 ETF Portfolio Manager Michael Monaghan told The Washington Post. He attributed investors’ supposedly souring mood on AI to Big Tech companies planning to double down on data center development amid a wave of politicians skeptical of such projects winning election in the 2026 midterms.

Monaghan also pointed to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation as another factor which may have influenced the apparent shift. (RELATED: What Jensen Huang’s Exit Could Mean For Washington’s Chip Controls)

SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk, who joined over 175,000 people in a petition to reinstate Huang, warned Nov. 14 that the resignation could be a blow to Nvidia.

“Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract,” Musk wrote on X. “Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.”

Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract. Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.

Nvidia’s board of directors is not planning to reinstate Huang after his affair with an alleged Chinese asset, CNBC, citing a person familiar with the matter, reported Monday.

Treasury Partners Chief Investment Officer Richard Saperstein also attributed the shifting mood to uncertainty concerning data centers, the outlet reported Friday.

“The stock market is going through an AI repricing, reflecting an environment of slowing data center buildouts, reduced funding sources for AI-related projects and a slower trajectory of technology-related earnings growth,” Saperstein told CNBC.

The shift comes despite Anthropic’s $81 billion initial public offering (IPO) and President Donald Trump’s bullish stance on AI and the data centers that provide AI models their computing power.

Trump wrote on Truth Social in August that “the only reason” communities throughout the U.S. wouldn’t want data centers is because they want to become “backwards and poor.”

“If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign,” Trump continued. “The good news is that there are plenty of other places that want them. If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement.”

Over 70% of Americans oppose data centers being built near their community, according to a Gallup poll published in May.

Trump also said during a White House press conference Friday that he may impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that esatblish data centers abroad, warning that China may take them if they do. The threat came after he returned from his summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The White House did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment.

تصویر نه از داستان (عکس از JOHANNES EISELE/AFP از طریق گتی ایماژ)
پس از اینکه شاخص نزدک کامپوزیت تمام رشدهای سال 2026 خود را در روز جمعه از دست داد، بسیاری از تحلیلگران وال استریت افت بازارها را به خطرات ذاتی در دوام مالی سرمایه گذاری های هوش مصنوعی نسبت دادند. واشنگتن پست گزارش داد، بازارهای سهام هفته را در میان بزرگترین فروش از زمان تعرفه های روز آزادی آوریل 2025 رئیس جمهور دونالد ترامپ به پایان رساندند. Nasdaq تنها در روز جمعه 5.28 درصد سقوط کرد، در حالی که S&P 500 و Dow Jones Industrial Average حداقل 8 درصد در طول هفته افت کردند. پس از ورود به قلمرو تصحیح، شاخص ها هر کدام حداقل 10 درصد از اوج های اخیر کاهش یافته اند.
